history.dynasty: Portuguese colonial period; renovated under later patronage
history.summary: Legend holds the deity was originally installed by Rama at Rameshwar after Lanka, and the Goa temple was built at Loutolim in Salcette by Gaud Saraswat Brahmins who had migrated from Rameshwar. To escape Portuguese destruction, the idol was shifted in 1566 to Ramnathim in Bandora (then Bandivade), which was under Bijapur control; the temple completed 450 years at its present site in May 2011. It follows the Panchayatana pattern: the chief Ramnath shrine surrounded by subsidiary shrines of Lakshmi Narayan, Siddhinath (Ganesh), Betal, plus idols of Shantadurga (brought from Rivona) and Kamakshi (from Loutolim). Features include a five-storied deepstambha and an ornate silver screen at the sanctum door. name: Shri Ramnath Temple
town_description: Ramnathim is a village in Bandora, Ponda taluka, North Goa, named after the deity Ramnath. It sits in Goa's temple heartland near the Shantadurga temple at Kavlem, about 7 km from Ponda and 28 km from Panaji.
tradition: Hindu (Shaiva Panchayatana; kuladevata of Goud Saraswat and Daivadnya Brahmins)

travel.railway: Karmali (nearest); Margao ~21 km; Vasco da Gama ~35 km
travel.road: At Ramnathim, Bandora, ~7 km from Ponda; 28 km from Panaji Kadamba Bus Stand via NH 748
